text:
**For a 1,000Wh power station, plan on about 200W of solar for a recharge in a day and a half, or about 300-400W for a full recharge in one sunny day.** Your location, the season and the station's solar input limit change that.

**The math**

Daily solar energy is panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

| Panel | Daily output at 4.5 sun hours (70%) | Time to refill 1,000Wh from empty |
|---|---|---|
| 100W | ~315Wh | ~3 days |
| 200W | ~630Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400W | ~1,260Wh | under a day |

Source: [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)

For a full recharge in one day, [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) gives these panel sizes for 1,000Wh:
- **6 sun hours:** about 230W
- **5 sun hours:** about 270W
- **4 sun hours:** about 340W
- **3 sun hours:** about 450W

[Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) estimates about 300W on a good summer day and 700W or more in a northern winter.

**Before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. A 200W limit means a bigger panel won't charge faster, though it can help in weak light ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage window:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within the station's input range. Going over can damage the charge controller ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Loads:** If you run devices while charging, net charging is slower.

**One option, if your station accepts it**

The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is $299 at ALLPOWERS's US store. The code ALLPOWERS26 takes it to $269.10 and expires 2026-12-30. The listing says it was tested in the store's cart on 2026-10-21, and checkout has the final word.
- **Specs:** 400W, Voc 45.3V, MC4 connectors with XT60 and DC adapters included.
- **Compatibility:** It suits 12-60V solar inputs. It's too high-voltage for stations limited to about 24-28V.
- **Weight:** It weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel.
- **Fit:** At 400W it only makes sense if your station accepts 400W of solar input. If your limit is 200W, a 200W panel is the better buy.
- **Returns:** The 30-day return window excludes sale items, and you pay return shipping unless the item is defective.
- **Affiliate link:** Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through its link.
